name: GI, Liver & Nutrition
sub: Variceal bleed, pancreatitis, liver failure, feeding, SUP

cards.q: Outline the management of acute variceal haemorrhage.
cards.a: Resuscitate with restrictive transfusion (Hb 7–8 g/dL), vasoactive drug (terlipressin or octreotide), antibiotic prophylaxis (ceftriaxone 1 g/day), and endoscopic band ligation within 12 hours; balloon tamponade or TIPS if refractory.

cards.q: When is prophylactic TIPS considered?
cards.a: Pre-emptive TIPS within 72 hours in high-risk patients (Child–Pugh C 10–13 or Child B with active bleeding at endoscopy).

cards.q: How is spontaneous bacterial peritonitis diagnosed and treated?
cards.a: Ascitic fluid neutrophils ≥250/mm³. Treat with IV cefotaxime or ceftriaxone and albumin 1.5 g/kg on day 1 and 1 g/kg on day 3.

cards.q: Name the grades of hepatic encephalopathy (West Haven).
cards.a: I: mild confusion, sleep disturbance. II: lethargy, asterixis. III: somnolent but rousable. IV: coma. Treat with lactulose, rifaximin, and correction of precipitants.

cards.q: What are the King's College criteria for liver transplant in paracetamol-induced acute liver failure?
cards.a: Arterial pH <7.30 after resuscitation, or all of: INR >6.5, creatinine >300 µmol/L (3.4 mg/dL) and grade III–IV encephalopathy.

cards.q: What is the dosing for N-acetylcysteine in paracetamol overdose?
cards.a: IV: 150 mg/kg over 1 hour, then 50 mg/kg over 4 hours, then 100 mg/kg over 16 hours (total 21 hours). Start within 8 hours for best protection; continue if ALT or INR still rising.

cards.q: How do you grade the severity of acute pancreatitis?
cards.a: Revised Atlanta: mild (no organ failure), moderately severe (transient organ failure <48 h or local complications), severe (persistent organ failure >48 h).

cards.q: What is the recommended fluid strategy in acute pancreatitis?
cards.a: Moderate goal-directed fluid therapy with lactated Ringer's (e.g. 1.5 mL/kg/h after a 10 mL/kg bolus if hypovolaemic); avoid aggressive hydration (WATERFALL).

cards.q: When is enteral feeding started in critically ill adults?
cards.a: Within 24–48 hours once haemodynamically stable; use enteral over parenteral unless contraindicated; target 20–25 kcal/kg/day initially and 1.2–2.0 g/kg protein.

cards.q: What is the stress ulcer prophylaxis recommendation?
cards.a: Give PPI or H2 blocker to patients with high bleeding risk (mechanical ventilation >48 h, coagulopathy, shock); SUP-ICU and REVISE showed small or no mortality differences.

cards.q: What features define abdominal compartment syndrome?
cards.a: IAP >20 mmHg with new organ dysfunction; grades I–IV by pressure (12–15, 16–20, 21–25, >25 mmHg).

cards.q: How is upper GI bleeding managed initially?
cards.a: Two large-bore IV lines, resuscitation, restrictive transfusion (Hb <7), high-dose PPI, early endoscopy within 24 hours, and risk scoring (Glasgow-Blatchford).

cards.q: What is the treatment of Clostridioides difficile infection?
cards.a: Fidaxomicin 200 mg twice daily for 10 days (preferred) or vancomycin 125 mg four times daily; fulminant: vancomycin 500 mg four times daily with IV metronidazole, with surgical review.

cards.q: What is the SOFA liver component?
What are the red flags for acute mesenteric ischaemia?
cards.a: Pain out of proportion to examination, lactic acidosis, atrial fibrillation or low-flow state. Obtain CT angiography early; surgical or endovascular revascularisation.

cards.q: How do you prevent aspiration in enterally fed ventilated patients?
cards.a: Head of bed 30–45°, check tube position, use prokinetics (metoclopramide, erythromycin) for intolerance, and consider post-pyloric feeding if gastric feeding fails.

cards.q: What is the definition of refeeding hypophosphataemia threshold?
cards.a: Serum phosphate falling by more than about 30% or to <0.65 mmol/L after feeding starts, requiring supplementation and calorie reduction.

cards.q: Which vitamin deficiencies matter in ICU alcohol withdrawal?
cards.a: Thiamine (Wernicke's): give 200–500 mg IV three times daily before glucose; also replace magnesium, potassium and folate.

cards.q: A cirrhotic patient bleeds from varices. Besides endoscopy, which drugs should be started immediately?
o: Terlipressin or octreotide plus IV ceftriaxone
cards.e: Vasoactive agents reduce portal pressure and antibiotic prophylaxis lowers infection and mortality in variceal bleeding.

cards.q: Ascitic fluid in a febrile cirrhotic shows 420 neutrophils/mm³. What is the best management?
cards.e: PMN ≥250/mm³ is SBP: treat with an antibiotic and albumin to reduce renal failure and mortality.
